text:
alex: FYI seeing a sharp p99 CPU + latency bump on a handful of hosts after the "parse-pulse" change landed to slim the parse layer. p50 unchanged, p99 ~3.5x. reproduces in staging with streaming clients. flamegraph attached: https://perf.internal/runs/3461/flame.html

maya: dug into a 60s pprof CPU from one affected host. top consumers show: proto.Unmarshal, runtime.mallocgc, and syscall writev. lots of tiny syscall bursts.

sasha: interesting — proto.Unmarshal alloc profile shows lots of small allocations for repeated submessages. we changed the grpc framing earlier which reduced packet coalescing; now each token frame is being sent separately -> many small writev syscalls.

alex: exact trace snippet from the profile (top stacks):
```
proto.(*Decoder).Unmarshal -> runtime.mallocgc -> runtime.mstart -> syscall.writev
net/http.(*conn).Write -> grpc.(*serverStream).SendMsg -> runtime.morestack
```

pranay: i reproduced locally with a wrk script hitting the streaming rpc:
```
w rk -t2 -c40 -d60 --latency 'http://staging-ingress/llm.stream' -s tools/stream_replay.lua
```
When I toggle the gateway coalesce window from 1ms -> 8ms p99 drops back to baseline. so coalescing looks like the biggest immediate win.

maya: confirmed. coalescing reduces writev syscall rate by ~70% in my run. p99 latency down ~2.8x.

sasha: KV cache note: the parse-pulse change shifts sequence length distribution slightly (more small prefix frames), which increased KV cache churn on some hot shards. eviction + cache-miss latency means more bytes get streamed in more chunks -> feedback loop.

alex: oof. so two interacting issues: (1) framing/coalesce regression -> many small writes; (2) shifted request shape -> kvcache thrash -> more small frames.

pranay: proposed short-term mitigations: rollback parse-pulse change OR enable transient gateway coalesce = 8ms, AND apply a soft throttle so KV hot-shard read concurrency is limited to avoid thrash.

maya: i opened a tiny patch to gateway that groups frames < 2KB for 8ms and then flushes (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4123). test harness shows improved p99 but needs load testing on dedicated.

deploy-bot: deploy started: gateway/coalesce-patch -> staging -> 5 hosts. status: 2/5 succeeded, 3/5 rolling. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4123

sasha: longer-term we should: switch to streaming proto.Decoder to avoid full unmarshalling copies for small repeated messages, and add unit microbench for proto decode allocs. also add an ingress-level sampler that coalesces writes from the same connection automatically when under backpressure.

alex: agree. action items i captured: [1] revert or keep coalesce until we have microbench (short term) (assigned: maya), [2] add proto decode microbench + fix (sasha), [3] add kvcache read concurrency cap per shard (pranay), [4] add e2e perf test that simulates many small streaming frames and asserts syscall/writev rate (alex).

maya: quick log from the staging run after coalesce patch:
```
before: writev syscalls/s = 8200, p99=320ms
after:  syscalls/s = 2400, p99=95ms  :thumbsup:
```

pranay: re: kvcache — i measured hot-shard QPS: before change ~600/s, after ~1100/s (because smaller frames increase request count). evictions went from 2/s -> 18/s. capping concurrent reads to 16 drops eviction to ~4/s and overall latency down.

alex: sounds like immediate rollout of gateway coalesce + kvcache cap is the right mitigation while sasha works on the decoder allocs. anyone object to promote the gate patch to dedicated canary?

maya: no objections. i'll coordinate the canary rollout and add the e2e.

sasha: i'll sketch the streaming-decoder PR and a microbenchmark today, link soon.

alex: thanks. also let's add a tracing tag for "coalesce-window-ms" so we can correlate future regressions quickly.

deploy-bot: deploy complete: gateway/coalesce-patch -> canary group (dedicated) -> success 3/3.

maya: leaving notes in the RFC doc: https://docs.internal/rw/inference/parse-pulse-investigation.md :sos: (summary + perf numbers + followups).

alex: excellent. follow-ups: sasha microbench, pranay kvcap cap PR, maya rollout + e2e. i'll open a tracking ticket to avoid regressions.

sasha: quick FYI — proto streaming decoder bench shows 6x fewer allocs and ~30% CPU less on decode path. will open PR tomorrow.

alex: great thread — thanks everyone :raised_hands:
